papers.title: Deciding when to stop: Efficient stopping of active learning guided drug-target prediction
papers.abstract: Active learning has shown to reduce the number of experiments needed to obtain high-confidence drug-target predictions. However, in order to actually save experiments using active learning, it is crucial to have a method to evaluate the quality of the current prediction and decide when to stop the experimentation process. Only by applying reliable stoping criteria to active learning, time and costs in the experimental process can be actually saved. We compute active learning traces on simulated drug-target matrices in order to learn a regression model for the accuracy of the active learner. By analyzing the performance of the regression model on simulated data, we design stopping criteria for previously unseen experimental matrices. We demonstrate on four previously characterized drug effect data sets that applying the stopping criteria can result in upto 40% savings of the total experiments for highly accurate predictions.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究药物靶点预测中的主动学习停止策略，与骨植入物力学仿真的代理建模和优化完全不相关。
llm.why_not_core: No FEA, surrogate modeling, constraint handling, uncertainty quantification, or any biomedical mechanics context; purely a machine learning method for drug discovery.

summary_zh.motivation: 减少药物靶点预测中主动学习的实验次数，提高效率。
summary_zh.method: 在模拟数据上训练回归模型预测主动学习精度，设计停止准则。
summary_zh.result: 在四个药物数据集上实现高达40%的实验节约，预测高度准确。
summary_zh.validation: 在模拟数据和真实药物效应数据集上验证停止准则效果。

summary_en.motivation: Reduce experimental costs in drug-target prediction by developing reliable stopping criteria for active learning.
summary_en.method: Train a regression model on simulated active learning traces to predict prediction accuracy and design stopping criteria.
summary_en.result: Apply the stopping criteria to four drug effect datasets, achieving up to 40% reduction in experiments while maintaining high accuracy.
summary_en.validation: Validation performed on simulated data and four real drug effect datasets.
